title: Quantum Resources and Wigner Symmetry in Nucleon-Nucleon Scattering from Effective Field Theory
authors: Ian Low, Thomas R. Richardson, Sokratis Trifinopoulos
abstract: We study quantum resources in the spin degrees of freedom, such as entanglement, stabilizer magic, and non-local magic, in low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering through next-to-leading order in pionless effective field theory. Treating each nucleon spin as a qubit, we calculate the corresponding resource-generating powers of the scattering operator at generic center-of-mass momentum and scattering angle $Θ$. The analysis retains $S$- and $P$-wave channels generated by two-derivative contact interactions. When the microscopic physics exhibits Wigner's $SU(4)$ spin-flavor symmetry, the neutron-proton amplitude becomes proportional to the spin-space identity operator and therefore generates no new resources after scattering, extending an observation previously made for leading-order $S$-wave scattering. The same-nucleon channel remains resource-generating because constraints from identical particles project out part of the Hilbert space. These results show how enhanced symmetries, partial-wave structure, and resource generation are intertwined in low-energy two-body scattering.
summary: This work analyzes quantum resources like entanglement in low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering using Effective Field Theory. It demonstrates that enhanced Wigner symmetry suppresses resource generation in $np$ scattering, while Pauli exclusion maintains it in $nn$ scattering. The study successfully connects fundamental symmetries and partial wave structure to measurable quantum information properties.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum resources, such as entanglement and magic power, are generated during low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering.
main_result: Wigner's SU(4) symmetry causes the neutron-proton amplitude to generate no new quantum resources, while the identical-nucleon channel remains resource-generating due to Pauli exclusion constraints.
method: The authors calculate resource measures (entanglement power, magic power) by analyzing the scattering operator acting on spin qubits within the framework of pionless effective field theory.
model_or_system: The system is low-energy nucleon-nucleon ($	ext{NN}$) scattering ($np$ and $nn$) analyzed using next-to-leading order pionless Effective Field Theory ($	ext{EFT}_{\pi/	ext{}}$). Spin degrees of freedom are treated as qubits.
key_observables: Entanglement power, stabilizer magic power, non-local magic power, and partial wave couplings ($A(L	ext{State})$).
important_parameters: Low center-of-mass momentum ($p$), scattering angle ($\Theta$), and EFT parameters like scattering lengths and effective ranges.
main_assumptions: The analysis extends previous studies to include P-waves (NLO in $	ext{EFT}_{\pi/	ext{}}$) and compares physical results against the idealized Wigner SU(4) symmetry limit.
figures_summary: Figures compare entanglement power ($E$) and magic power ($\mathcal{M}$) for $np 	o np$ and $nn 	o nn$ channels, contrasting physical predictions (solid lines) with Wigner-symmetric benchmarks (dashed lines).
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the resource measures within EFT, analyzes the impact of Wigner symmetry on partial wave couplings, and compares the resulting quantum resource generation in the $np$ vs. $nn$ channels.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete physical system (nuclear scattering) where fundamental symmetries dictate the capacity for generating non-classical correlations, linking nuclear structure theory to quantum information diagnostics.
